instruction: Make the title text italic and type 'Study Abroad Guide' in the text placeholder below the title.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully changed slide background to purple and added title text to notes in LibreOffice Impress.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open color picker, set background color, navigate to notes panel, type text, select text and apply formatting.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests text formatting (italic) and text entry skills, which are related to the original task's text manipulation capabilities.
metadata.explanation: Getter checks if title runs have italic=True and if the subtitle placeholder contains 'Study Abroad Guide'. Metric gives 0.5 for italic title and 0.5 for correct subtitle text (case-insensitive substring match).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly identifies the title shape by matching known text 'Should You Consider Studying Abroad' and checks font.italic on the first run.
Getter correctly captures the subtitle text from the first non-title text shape, which is appropriate for a standard Impress title slide layout.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_subtitle') without incorrectly nesting into 'rules'.
Both instruction requirements are verified: italic title (0.5 points) and subtitle text (0.5 points) with sensible partial credit.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Minor concern: getter only checks italic on the first run of the title. If the title has multiple runs with mixed formatting, it could give a false positive. This is unlikely in practice but not fully robust.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking italic status on all runs in the title shape to ensure the entire title is italic, not just the first run.
